$description: EIJA Studio spacing, size, border, focus and radius tokens. DTCG Format Module 2025.10 (Final Community Group Report, not a W3C Standard; opened 2026-09-29 at https://www.designtokens.org/tr/2025.10/format/). Every value is a DESIGN_TARGET (our hypothesis) unless its extension record says LITERATURE_LIMIT (a published threshold) or DERIVED (arithmetic on other tokens). Nothing here is a measurement of users. Density numbers follow the layout aspect (docs/hci/design/layout-model.md section 3.5, HCI-ADR-0058), which owns density; this file owns the names. Decision record: docs/adr/0068-hci-design-system-architecture.md. Design document: docs/hci/design/design-system-architecture.md. Colour and type tokens are in color.tokens.json and typography.tokens.json (other aspects).

io.github.45ck.eija-studio.unit-policy: Spacing and control sizes are rem so they follow the user's default font size; border widths and radii are px so a hairline stays one CSS pixel. Tests convert rem to px at a 16 px root (assumption A-ROOT: the Studio never sets html font-size). Tokens here are DTCG dimensions {value, unit} with px or rem, the only units DTCG 2025.10 allows.
io.github.45ck.eija-studio.scale-rule: space.N is N x 4 px. Eight steps, no half steps. A gap or padding in shipped CSS must be one of these or 0 (test DS-05).
io.github.45ck.eija-studio.baseline-measured: Distinct px values in padding, margin and gap declarations of src/eija_studio/resources/web/app.css, counted by script on 2026-09-29: see docs/hci/design/design-system-architecture.md section 5.1.
io.github.45ck.eija-studio.mode-contract: Groups size.control, size.field, size.row, size.chip and size.icon carry a default and a compact value. index.tokens.json maps the semantic density.* names to them per density mode. Both modes must have the same key set (test DS-06). The compact values are written under [data-density="compact"] through the semantic density.* tokens in index.tokens.json (which carry the Terrazzo-style mode key, kept as a tool-specific key until resolver support is tested).
io.github.45ck.eija-studio.density-source: docs/hci/design/layout-model.md section 3.5: chrome control and row 28 / 24, typed-answer field 32 / 28, chip 24 / 20 (non-interactive only), gutter 12 to 16 / 8. The accessibility design (docs/hci/design/accessibility.md D5) says default density 32; the layout aspect owns density and its numbers are used. The conflict is listed in design-system-architecture.md section 14.

space.$description: Gap, padding and margin scale. Proximity encodes grouping before any border does (Gestalt proximity; rubric: containers only where they encode grouping or state).

1.$description: 4 px. Glyph to its word; inline gaps inside one label.

2.$description: 8 px. Items of one group; chip padding; gap between a row's cells.

3.$description: 12 px. Row padding along the reading axis; label to field.

4.$description: 16 px. Between related groups; padding of a region.

8.$description: 32 px. Between regions of one view.

16.$description: 64 px. Largest step. Reserved for first-run and empty views; not used in the working views.

size.$description: Interactive target and row sizes in two density modes. Compact never goes below the 24 px floor for an interactive target.

hit-min.$description: 24 px. Floor for the smaller side of any pointer target. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), Level AA: at least 24 by 24 CSS px unless a listed exception applies (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html, opened 2026-09-29). Exceptions: spacing, equivalent, inline, user-agent control, essential. The design system uses two of them and no others: spacing for the seam only (content inset 12 px from its centre line in both densities) and inline for links inside running text only (test DS-07, docs/hci/design/design-system-architecture.md sections 5.4 and 10.2). Every other interactive element meets the floor.

default.$description: 28 px. Button, tab, filter field and other chrome controls in the default density (layout-model.md section 3.5).

compact.$description: 24 px. Compact density sits exactly on the WCAG floor and never below it.

default.$description: 32 px. Fields that take typed answers: decision dialog, rename, definition.

compact.$description: 28 px. Typed-answer field in the compact density.

default.$description: 28 px. Tree row, list row and table row in the default density.
24 px. Chip height. An interactive chip reads this value directly in both densities (not density.chip-height, whose compact value is 20 px).

compact.$description: 20 px. Non-interactive chips only (layout-model.md section 3.5). DS-07 fails an interactive element below the floor.

default.$description: 16 px. Status glyph and action glyph box, one size for both. The canvas aspect assumes a 16 px status slot on each node.

compact.$description: 16 px. Same as default: a glyph below 16 px is not drawn (status shapes must stay distinct, P6).

border.$description: Line widths in px so that a hairline is one CSS pixel at any root font size.

hairline.$description: Separators, control outlines, the second elevation step (surface step plus 1 px border; dark-mode shadows are near invisible, see docs/hci/research/visual-design-foundations.md section 2.5).

strong.$description: Selected state and keyboard focus ring. A second, non-colour cue for selection.

offset.$description: Gap between a focused element and its ring so the ring does not touch the element's own border.

inset.$description: Negative offset: the focus ring is drawn inside the element. Used for tree rows, list rows, tabs and anything inside a scroll container, where an outer ring is clipped (docs/hci/design/accessibility.md D6, MEASURED there in Chrome 154).

radius.$description: Two radii only. The baseline uses six distinct non-zero radii (MEASURED, docs/hci/design/design-system-architecture.md section 5.1).

1.$description: Controls, chips, table cells with outlines.

2.$description: Floating surfaces: dialog, popover, palette. Never a container inside a container.
